public_rationale: The heart of this claim is that ChatGPT was the only generative AI 'killer app' or 'industry-defining product' two years into the boom. Those are judgment words with no stated measure. Reasonable readers could count or exclude other products, such as coding assistants or image generators, and no record settles that. The side point that ChatGPT burns billions is consistent with reporting that OpenAI expected to lose about $5 billion in 2024 (e1). But that cannot carry the main proposition. 'Nobody can really describe' it is rhetoric. So the claim is not scored.
limitations: The OpenAI loss figure covers the whole company, not ChatGPT alone, and was a projection when reported.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Two years into the boom, generative AI has no killer apps other than ChatGPT, which burns billions.

statement.excerpt: We're two years in, and we have no killer apps — no industry-defining products — other than ChatGPT, a product that burns billions of dollars and nobody can really describe.

from_speaker: no killer apps — no industry-defining products — other than ChatGPT
a product that burns billions of dollars
our_interpretation: The core of the claim is that no generative AI product other than ChatGPT counts as a 'killer app' or 'industry-defining product'. He gives no measure for either term (users, revenue, market share, or impact).
Which products count as 'killer apps' is a value judgment. Informed readers could reasonably disagree about products like coding assistants or image generators, and no public record settles that.

The sub-claim that ChatGPT 'burns billions' can be checked against reporting on OpenAI's 2024 losses. 'Nobody can really describe' it is rhetoric. Since the main proposition has no plain, testable reading, the claim as a whole is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Would need an agreed, measurable definition of 'killer app' under which only ChatGPT qualified by December 2024, plus evidence that ChatGPT/OpenAI lost billions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would need an agreed, measurable definition of 'killer app' under which another generative AI product clearly qualified by December 2024, or evidence that ChatGPT/OpenAI did not lose billions.
